speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and a rash of small red spots called petechiae. To understand the cause of this bleeding disorder, can you tell me if you have had any easy bruising, bleeding gums, or if there is a family history of similar bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presentation of frequent epistaxis, gingival bleeding, petechiae on the extremities, and easy bruising in a 4-year-old male is highly characteristic of ITP, likely following a recent viral infection. I will order a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with peripheral smear to confirm isolated thrombocytopenia. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Peripheral_Smear
